title: Nextcloud sync clients poll instead of being pushed changes
body:
`blueprints/nextcloud-s3-oidc/` (`services.yml`, `x-catena.yml`, `test.yml`). The app runs no notify_push (Client Push)
service, so every desktop and mobile client polls the server for changes, which costs CPU and database load per client.
notify_push is a Nextcloud app plus a push server shipped as a binary in the app; the server listens on 7867, reads
`config.php` (or `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL`, `NEXTCLOUD_URL`), needs Redis, and is set up with
`occ app:enable notify_push` then `occ notify_push:setup https://<host>/push`, which runs its own checks
([README](https://github.com/nextcloud/notify_push)). Its troubleshooting covers the push server needing to be a trusted
proxy (`trusted_proxies`, `HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR` in `forwarded_for_headers`). At pick-up: which image runs the binary (the
Nextcloud image with the app's binary, or a published one) and how `/push/` on the app's hostname reaches it with
WebSocket upgrade.

- **Behaviour:** a Nextcloud install runs the push service by default; sync clients receive changes without polling, and
  the app's settings page shows Client Push configured.
- **Security notes:** a new WebSocket route `/push/` on the app's public hostname; the push service holds the same
  database and Redis credentials as Nextcloud.
- **Acceptance:** `app-tests` for nextcloud-s3-oidc passes a leg where `occ notify_push:setup https://<host>/push`

title: The catalog's generated files render after a merge, not in each import pull request
body:
The importer feed is built: adapters for Lissy93's and Portainer's lists, Arcane's registry, the per-app template
directory and awesome-selfhosted (project facts only); sources read at pinned commits; deduplication by image repository
and upstream repository with alias records; the copied collection's licence recorded with its notice, and the app's own
licence checked against MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, GPL, LGPL and AGPL; `--entry` to import chosen entries. Imports go through
the app-add agent, one `import/<id>` pull request in flight at a time (decided 2026-11-15: no scheduled waves). Every
import pull request re-renders `catalog.json` and `index.html`, so merging one forces the others to re-render.

- **Behaviour:** the generated files (`catalog.json`, `index.html`) are rendered after a merge to main instead of in
  each import pull request, so two app pull requests never conflict in a generated file. No scheduled workflow opens
  import waves; the wave settings (5 a day, 10 open) are removed.
- **Security notes:** none beyond app-ci and app-tests.
- **Acceptance:** two import pull requests merge one after the other without a conflict in a generated file; main's
  generated files match a fresh render after each merge (`render-idempotency`). Workflow edits need a person with the
  Workflows permission.

title: Talk's media server needs the relay

title: Nextcloud's call server runs only while the call relay app runs
body:
`blueprints/nextcloud/` (talk-hpb in `services.yml` and `docker-compose.yml`; the Talk wiring in `hooks/configure.sh`).
The talk-hpb service (signaling server, Janus, NATS, bundled eturnal) runs and is routed publicly at
`${SIGNALING_HOSTNAME}`, with no sign-in gate, on every Nextcloud. The configure hook points Talk at it only when the call
relay app provides `TURN_HOSTNAME` and `TURN_SECRET`; without the relay, Talk keeps its peer-to-peer mode and the service
only costs memory and exposes an endpoint nobody calls.

- **Behaviour (decided 2026-11-15):** the call server runs, and gets its public name, only while the call relay app
  runs, keyed on observed state (the relay running), never a flag. Without the relay, Talk stays peer-to-peer and no
  talk-hpb task or route exists; when the relay is added, the next deploy brings talk-hpb and the configure hook points
  Talk at it; when the relay is removed, talk-hpb and its route go. The package's notes (EN/FR) say so.
- **Security notes:** no public endpoint without a call it serves. The signaling server checks every caller itself.
- **Acceptance:** the Nextcloud app-tests cover both cases: without the relay, no talk-hpb task and no
  `${SIGNALING_HOSTNAME}` route; with the relay, Talk uses the call server and a three-participant call works.

Moved from catenahq/ops#396. Replaces catenahq/catena-templates#303 (the call server carrying media without the relay is
